newsitem.title: USA: CSCE July coffee jumps to new lifetime high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE July coffee jumps to new lifetime high.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices bounded higher in afternoon trading Monday, with benchmark July surging to a new life-of-contract high, as speculators went on a buying spree amid ongoing supply concerns, traders said.
Most-active July futures soared to a lifetime of 229.50 cents per lb as of 1321 EDT, up 11.60 cents. Spot May rose 6.00 cents, to 245.00, while the back months traded 3.95 to 9.45 higher.

Traders said bullish sentiment was fueled by a report from brokerage Merrill Lynch, which said coffee prices could reach record highs ahead of new crop shipments this autumn due to continued supply tightness.
Although Merrill Lynch did not specify a price, the highest price on CSCE was 340.70 cents a lb set April 14, 1977.

Additionally, news a Colombian exporter said the country's 1996/97 coffee harvest was likely to fall short of the federation's estimate of about 10.1 million bags also bolstered the market, traders said.
The private exporter, who did not wish to be named, told Reuters that based on production figures so far, he forecast this year's output at some 9.5 million bags.
His estimate took into consideration April to June production projection of around 2.5 million bags, down from the federation's forecast of three million 60-kg bags for that period.
